newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico peso ends mixed on pre-weekend swaps.
newsitem.headline: Mexico peso ends mixed on pre-weekend swaps.

text.p: The Mexican peso closed mixed on Friday due to pre-weekend swap trading but was firmer than in earlier dealings, as local and foreign brokers sold dollars to invest in the money market, traders said.
"High interest rates encouraged portfolio investors to step into Mexico," a trader said.
The benchmark 48-hour peso ended 0.8 of a centavo firmer at 7.8670/7.8695 per dollar, while its 24-hour stablemate was 0.1 of a centavo weaker at 7.8630/7.8660.
Same-day peso contracts had earlier closed 0.9 of a centavo firmer at 7.8570/7.8610 per dollar.
Dealers said demand for money market paper could be seen in overnight Cetes rates, that were down 60 basis points to 23.50 percent in late trade.
"I feel the peso will hold steady until Tuesday," another trader said. "It depends on what Banco de Mexico does with interest rates next week."
Some traders said the peso did not gain further ground against the dollar on Friday because some banks exercised dollar puts previously auctioned by the central bank.
